_comment: PER-VOICE DELIVERY TUNING — one row per conditioning sample in the pool.
Two knobs, both 0..1, both optional. Omit either one and it falls through to
the pool-wide default in tuning.json:
exaggeration  base-model emotion intensity. On this pool it is the PACE and
expression knob together: 0.45 -> 0.75 measured +11% words per
second and +44% pitch range. It peaks near 0.75; past ~0.8 the
model destabilises and reads SLOWER and flatter, not faster.
cfgWeight     style-adherence weight. NOT a speed control despite the folk
wisdom: dropping it 0.55 -> 0.30 measured 12% SLOWER here.
Keep it mid, 0.50 to 0.62.
Set these when a particular sample reads badly at the default — too slow, too
flat, too hot. The setting moves every character cast on that voice at once,
which is the point: pace is a property of the SAMPLE, and the same numbers do
not land the same way on two different speakers.
PRECEDENCE, most specific first:
characters.json  a performance one character wants (overrides this file)
voices.json      this file: how the sample reads by default
tuning.json      the pool-wide fallback
Both layers feed the resumption stamp, so editing a row here re-speaks exactly
the takes it affects on the next pass. No --fresh needed.
f0 is the measured median fundamental frequency, written by audition.mts. It
is reference only and nothing reads it; lower is deeper.
Audition a change before committing to it:
npx tsx tools/voice/audition.mts <voice> --tune 0.78,0.55
